headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad egress and API use create leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are lower due to limited overlap with langchain4j.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no network egress and no shared I/O surfaces, while B can run browsers and process files/logs. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so direct injection is not default. Risk remains low because B may ingest externally sourced content and A is a library that could be used to parse untrusted text if wired that way.
conditions: IF the operator wires A’s outputs into B’s browser or file-processing pipeline without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the agents, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste or file handoff between agents.
Sanitize any HTML/markdown before B consumes it.
Add a provenance label to all A-generated text.
requires-engineering: add content filtering at the orchestration layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B handles financial reports, research papers, logs, and broad API calls. The pair can still leak data if A is used to transform or route B’s sensitive inputs into prompts or logs. The pathway is plausible in default research workflows, though not proven by direct shared-storage evidence.
conditions: IF B processes financial reports or logs through external APIs, those contents may leave the local boundary.
IF A is used as a wrapper around B’s outputs, sensitive text can be copied into downstream prompts or logs.
mitigations: Restrict B to non-sensitive datasets.
Redact logs before any API call.
Store secrets outside shared working directories.
Review outbound prompts for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules on API payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes no write or network surfaces, while B has broad egress, browser access, and multiple-instance support. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource such as a shared filesystem or git state, so direct write conflict is not established. Uncertainty is low because the profiles do not show a shared writable target.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or log path, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable OAuth scope, resource conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Use per-agent credentials.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s research automation and browser/API use make it likely to act on upstream text, while A is a general LLM library that can generate or transform instructions. If A’s output is fed into B without verification, B may treat it as authoritative and propagate errors into reports or actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF A-generated text is inserted into B’s prompts or task plans without review, errors can cascade.
IF B auto-executes browser/API actions from A’s output, incorrect facts can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add a verification step for citations and facts.
Separate generation from execution roles.
Log source provenance for every instruction.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles financial reports, logs, and multiple external APIs plus secrets, creating a compliance-sensitive surface. A is a library with no egress, but pairing it with B can still route regulated or confidential data into third-party services. Because B’s default API-based workflow is dangerous for sensitive data and the profiles do not show a residency or DPA safeguard, high is warranted.
conditions: IF B processes EU PII, financial records, or secrets through external APIs without a DPA, compliance exposure occurs.
IF logs contain regulated data and are sent to third-party inference endpoints, retention and residency obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B’s inputs.
Use a compliant API tenant or region.
Rotate and scope secrets narrowly.
Review retention settings for logs.
requires-engineering: implement policy checks for residency and DPA requirements.
